newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power lackluster amid ample supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power lackluster amid ample supply.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. were flat to slightly weaker amid continued moderate weather and ample supplies, market sources said Wednesday.
"The market's softened up today. There seems to be a lot of excess energy to be sold," said a northern California trader.
Next-day firm on-peak power at the California-Oregon border (COB) was quoted $22.25-22.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $22.50-23.00 on Tuesday.
The Bonneville Power Administration continued to offer surplus sales at above-market prices of $26.00 for COB and $25.25 for Northwest deliveries.
Southwest prices were also slightly weaker with firm on-peak Palo Verde quoted $19.00-19.50 per MWh, down from $20.00-21.00.
"It's above 70 degrees (Fahrenheit) in Los Angeles and nice in Phoenix," noted another trader.
Traders said trade for cash December was also quiet today, with few physical deals seen.
December COB was notionally quoted at $23.00-23.50, compared with $22.80-23.15 on Tuesday. December Palo Verde was quoted at $21.15-21.40, compared with $20.75-21.30.
